data.narrative:
Marvel Fusion, a Series B nuclear energy company founded by Moritz von der Linden, has raised $400M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a sector universe of 11 peers: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, and Aalo Atomics.

A single triangulation method proved applicable. The stage-progression approach uses the $400M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage progression, yielding $760M. A peer-median analysis could not be executed: while four same-sector peers exist, the narrow filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, similar valuation tier) returned fewer than three datapoints—insufficient for robust cross-sectional support. Applying all-sector medians would introduce material bias.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $646M (low) to $874M (high), with a median of $760M. This range reflects the single applicable method; the narrow window reflects use of a consistent, stage-appropriate multiplier rather than broad peer triangulation. Key uncertainties include the true comparability of Marvel Fusion's technology and timeline to the identified peer set, the relevance of public-market multiples to private nuclear ventures, and execution risk inherent in the frontier nuclear sector. A peer-median cross-check becomes viable only upon identifying additional same-stage, similarly-scaled private comparables.
